review_notes: Independently read the complete current proposal.json, functionality.md, all 669 lines of fact-dispositions.json, all 176 lines of link-dispositions.json, both owned files in canonical and rendered forms, all 26 baseline subject records, all 69 baseline facts, and all eight outgoing links.

All four proposed fact writes are supported. They target owned functions, use allowed fact types and operations, and correctly separate literal x508 member-address behavior from intended reserved-ID reconstruction. The three registrar corrections accurately document unchecked null objects, count/occupancy divergence, preserved payloads on reset, and absent signed-overflow protection. No replacement proposal is supplied.
The repair requirement is confined to the malformed canonical citation in functionality.md. No additional fact write is required by this independent review.

Verified foreign definitions and consumers: ColorOverlay and registry declarations, callback typedef, installer and dispatcher, reserved-ID predicate, fighter and item material consumers, common-fighter light-object consumers, Hammer and healing cleanup, all three count-driven ftcoll consumers, startup reset placements, assertion macro branches, and demonstrated stage registrations/callbacks.
The light-object claim is supported: ftCo_8009F75C and ftCo_8009F7F8 call the selector and use its flags while configuring HSD lights. The earlier librarian deferral is no longer necessary.

The registry capacities are physical array capacities, not unconditional count bounds. Repeated null registrations can exceed them before any signed-overflow issue arises. Consumers index by counts, making the out-of-bounds risk concrete. This is not proof that an actual gameplay path supplies such inputs.

The callback ABI uncertainty is real: storage uses a three-argument Boolean callback, collision traversal passes an output descriptor address through a Vec3 pointer cast, and Mario's callback declares two arguments and returns zero. No portable universal callback compatibility is proved.

Boundary descriptions are supported: Dream Land uses ordered strict rectangle comparisons; Old Kongo uses strict squared-distance comparison; Mario uses strict current/previous threshold comparisons and conditionally scales particles after generator creation. These descriptions do not establish all possible parameter values or target floating-point modes.

Retained names are descriptive hypotheses, not recovered symbols. All section-subject facts and exact compiled x508 displacement claims remain specifically deferred. Existing links are retained only for their stated limited registration/query relationships.
